anomalies.observed: On the Peristaltic Pump Drivers sheet the pH-pump TMC2209 U7 coil outputs carry the same global labels as the pH isolated-I2C lines on the I2C Sensors sheet: U7 pin21 (OA2)=NET0097 and U7 pin26 (OB1)=NET0094, while U10 pin17/pin18 (the ADM3260 secondary SDA1/SCL1 that feed the EZO-pH M1) are also NET0094/NET0097. Likewise U4 pin26 (Nutrient-A coil OB1)=NET0086 is the same label as U6 pin16 (Nutrient-B STEP input)=NET0086. Per the connectivity rule (same label name = same net), the stepper motor phase/power outputs are shorted to the isolated pH I2C data/clock lines and to a STEP control line.
anomalies.expected: The intended design keeps these as separate nets: each EZO circuit sits on its own isolated-domain I2C pair (/SDA_pH,/SCL_pH) and each TMC2209 drives a 2-phase coil output (/A_xx,/B_xx) to its pump connector, with individual STEP lines kept distinct from coil/power nets. Motor phase outputs must not share a net with I2C data/clock or with a STEP control input.

anomalies.impact: The 24 V stepper coil drive voltages are tied directly to the pH sensor's isolated I2C bus and to a STEP input. This shorts unrelated buses together: the EZO-pH I2C lines and the Nutrient-B STEP line are loaded/driven by motor phase outputs, causing I2C corruption or lockup on the pH channel, erratic stepper stepping, and possible damage to the isolator/EZO and driver outputs. The board will not behave as intended.
